spots.name: Poznań Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sts. Apostles Peter and Paul Archcathedral Basilica in Poznań is one of the oldest churches in Poland and the oldest Polish cathedral, dating from the 10th century. It is the oldest historical monument in Poznań. It stands on the island of Ostrów Tumski north-east of the city centre.

spots.name: Poznań Główny
spots.summary: Poznań Główny lit. 'Poznań Main' is the main railway station of the city of Poznań, Poland's fifth-largest city, and capital of the Greater Poland Voivodeship.

spots.name: Imperial Castle, Poznań

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Imperial Castle in Poznań, popularly called Zamek, "the Castle", is a palace in Poznań, Poland. It was built under German rule in 1910 by Franz Schwechten for Wilhelm II, German Emperor, with substantial suggestions from the Emperor.

spots.name: Royal Castle, Poznań

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Royal Castle in Poznań dates from 1249 and the reign of Przemysł I. Located in the Polish city of Poznań, it was largely destroyed during the Second World War but has since been partly rebuilt.

spots.name: Poznań Town Hall
spots.summary: Poznań Town Hall is a historic city hall in the city of Poznań, Poland, located at the Poznań Old Town in the centre of the Old Market Square. It used to serve as the seat of local government until 1939, and now houses a museum.

spots.name: Citadel Park
spots.summary: The Citadel Park in Poznań, Poland is a large park on the site of Fort Winiary, a 19th-century fortified area north of the city centre. It contains a military museum, military cemeteries, and the remains of some of the fortifications. It lies within the Stare Miasto district of the city, south of Winogrady.

spots.name: Poznań Fara
spots.summary: The Basilica of Our Lady of Perpetual Help in Poznań Fara, also informally known as the Poznan Fara, is a Catholic minor basilica located in Poznań Old Town district of Poland.

spots.name: Old Market Square, Poznań
spots.summary: Old Market Place is the center and oldest part of the Old Town of Poznań, Poland. This market is the third largest market square in Poland, after Main Square in Kraków, and Market Square in Wrocław.

spots.name: Lake Malta
spots.summary: Lake Malta, known also as the Maltański Reservoir, is an artificial lake in Poznań, Poland. It was formed in 1952 as a result of the damming of the Cybina River. It is about 2.2 km long, which makes the lake the biggest man-made lake of the city. The water is 3.1 m deep on average with a maximum about 5 m.

spots.name: National Museum in Poznań

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The National Museum in Poznań, Poland, abbreviated MNP, is a state-owned cultural institution and one of the largest museums in Poland. It houses a rich collection of Polish painting from the 16th century on, and a collection of foreign painting.

spots.name: Fort VII

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Fort VII, officially Konzentrationslager Posen, was a Nazi concentration camps set up in Poznań in German-occupied Poland during World War II, located in one of the 19th-century forts circling the city.

spots.name: Poznań Old Zoo
spots.summary: The Poznań Old Zoo is one of the oldest zoological gardens in Poland, located in the city of Poznań, Greater Poland Voivodeship. It was founded in 1874 and was included on the register of objects of cultural heritage in 1978 as a unique example of a vivarium.

spots.name: Święty Marcin

spots.name: Poznań International Fair
spots.summary: The Poznań International Fair is the biggest industrial fair in Poland. It is held on the Poznań fairground in Poland. Poznań International Fair is located in the centre of the city opposite the main railway station – Poznań Główny, in the centre of Poland and in the centre of Europe.

spots.name: Działyński Palace
spots.summary: Działyński Palace in Poznań, Poland is a Baroque palace built in 1773 to 1776. The building features a rich stucco-decorated interior of its "Red Hall" and a classicist façade decorated with sculptures. The palace serves as one of the locations of Kórnik Library today.

spots.name: Pranger of Poznań
spots.summary: The Pranger of Poznań is found near the north-east corner of the Town Hall, not far from the Prozerpina Fountain. It is an eight-sided, late-Gothic column, on the summit of which stands a statue of an executioner in a Crusader's outfit holding a raised sword. The current pranger is a copy made by Marcin Rożek in 1925.

spots.name: Grand Theatre, Poznań
spots.summary: Grand Theatre, Poznań is a neoclassical opera house located in Poznań, Poland. It is named after famous Polish composer Stanisław Moniuszko.

spots.name: Poznańskie Krzyże
spots.summary: Poznań June 1956 Monument (Poznań Crosses) is a monument on Adam Mickiewicz Square in the Imperial District in Poznań, commemorating the 1956 Poznań protests and subsequent protests in the Polish People's Republic.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monument to the Victims of June 1956

spots.name: Lake Rusałka
spots.summary: Lake Rusałka is an artificial lake in Poznań, Poland. It has an area of 367,000 square metres. It was named after the water nymph Rusalka. It was formed in 1943 as a result of the damming of the Bogdanka River. In 1940 thousands of people were executed in the forests surrounding the lake.

spots.summary: New Synagogue is a synagogue located in Poznań at the corner of 17 Wroniecka Street and Stawna Street, near Rabbi Akiva Eger Square. It is currently the only freestanding synagogue remaining in Poznań.

spots.summary: Porta Posnania is an interactive heritage center in Poznań dedicated to the history of Cathedral Island the most ancient district of the city, in particular, the role that this place played in the times of the formation of the Polish Statehood. The opening took place on May 1, 2014.

spots.name: Enigma Cipher Centre

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Enigma Cipher Centre is an interactive multimedia exhibition in Poznan dedicated to the Enigma cipher machine and the three Polish cryptologists -- Marian Rejewski, Henryk Zygalski and Jerzy Rozycki—who played a key role in its early cryptanalysis. It is located in the former Collegium Historicum building.

spots.name: Raczyński Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Raczyński Library is a public library founded by Count Edward Raczyński in Poznań. The library's building was erected in 1822–1828 with the financial support of the Edward Raczyński Foundation. The structure of the classical building features a colonnade reminiscent of the eastern façade of the Louvre.

spots.name: Muzeum Literackie Henryka Sienkiewicza (Poznań, Poland)

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Sienkiewicz, who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1905, is best known for his work Quo Vadis?, an epic on early Christians in the Roman empire. He is Poland's most celebrated novelist, and this is the most extensive collection of items about his life and works.

spots.summary: The Lubrański Academy was a university college that was established in 1518 in Poznań by Bishop Jan Lubrański. It was the first school with university aspirations in Poznań.
